tasks.short: Explain changes to reports, tools and metric definitions to their users.

steps.what: Collect released changes from the {PROJECT}, {BI} and {DOCS}.
Identify affected users and communication priority from the report catalogue.
Write explanations, examples and migration instructions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved release facts, metric definitions, affected audiences and a guidance template.
loop.output: Report-change guidance linked to release facts.
loop.check: Check identifiers, dates and links automatically; the analyst approves accuracy and user impact.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per release; missing facts return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle routine notices; explaining varied metric changes needs short, audience-specific prose.

steps.what: Publish guidance in the {DOCS} and notify users through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Discuss confusing changes and collect user feedback.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} builds an enhancement register from approved releases in the {PROJECT} and report metadata in the {BI}. A recipient map and templates handle routine notices; a bounded drafting loop prepares complex guidance for analyst approval in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} publishes approved guidance and sends targeted notifications through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release facts, report ownership and guidance were maintained separately. Keeping audience mappings current often cost more than sending a broad notice.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release records, subscriptions and interfaces support most of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort; a small drafting loop handles varied explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies and report ownership can be incomplete. Users need human explanations when changes affect established decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which changes will confuse users and explain their practical consequences.

ambition.what: Report-change impact previews for budget holders before major metric changes.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling and sending notices and more time helping users adopt changes. Publishing authority stays within the existing release policy; no new financial decision rights arise.

reach.task: Explain how changed metric definitions affect budget variance interpretation.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, variance conventions and planning deadlines.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-8; 10-30 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Release-triggered templates, recipient mappings and internal notifications can use deterministic automation.
Typical steps, time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Most recipients are internal report users.
Approved releases have stable identifiers and accessible records.
Simple notices use templates without a model.
Build ranges cover one report estate and reuse existing identity controls.
GDPR applies to recipient records; employee consultation depends on the design and national rules.
unknowns: Completeness of report ownership and dependency records.
Available release, metadata and notification interfaces.
Who can approve guidance and publish internal notices.
Whether adoption tracking involves identifiable employee behaviour.
research_questions: Can existing subscriptions and release templates cover most notices?
Which recurring user questions require live explanation?
new_work: Review drafted guidance and audience exceptions.
Maintain report ownership and recipient mappings.
Handle failed notifications and outdated links.
Update templates when metric conventions change.

tasks.short: Test reports and datasets against business requirements and financial control totals.

steps.what: Agree expected decisions, definitions and acceptance criteria with the finance manager.
Translate acceptance criteria into test cases and expected results in the {DOCS}.
Run test queries and inspect report filters, totals and access in the {BI}.
Reconcile report totals with an export from the {ERP} in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Judge discrepancies and record defects or justified differences in the {PROJECT}.
Approve business acceptance or return the report for correction.

tasks.design: Structured acceptance criteria in the {DOCS} generate reusable test specifications for analyst approval. Deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} test the {BI}, reconcile totals against the {ERP} and attach evidence to defects in the {PROJECT}. The finance manager approves business acceptance before release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were expressed inconsistently, and test evidence was assembled separately from financial reconciliations. Automated checks could verify calculations without establishing business usefulness.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable criterion types, query interfaces and versioned datasets make repeatable checks practical. AI-assisted coding makes the test harness cheaper to build without putting a model in the calculation path.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous requirements, historical restatements and valid accounting differences need interpretation. Visual usability and whether a report supports the intended decision still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Define meaningful acceptance criteria and distinguish a defect from a legitimate business difference.

ambition.what: A financial-report regression evidence pack for every proposed release.

tasks.altitude: The analyst runs fewer repetitive checks and spends more time designing useful tests and resolving discrepancies. Business acceptance remains with the finance manager; the analyst gains no release authority automatically.

reach.task: Define reconciliation tolerances between management reports and ledger totals.
reach.learn: Posting cutoffs, consolidation adjustments and accounting materiality.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 10-30 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Calculation checks, reconciliation and regression tests can run deterministically against approved expectations.
Business usefulness and acceptable accounting differences require stakeholder judgment.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for a limited initial report set.

assumptions: The company already has financial reports, query access and a business acceptance process.
Repeatable criteria can be represented as measures, dimensions, tolerances and permission expectations.
Novel criteria remain manually authored; no language model is necessary initially.
Test evidence uses minimised data and existing GDPR access controls.
Consultation requirements depend on employee data use and national rules.
unknowns: Existing test automation and whether configuration can replace custom code.
Availability of stable test datasets and ledger control totals.
Supported interfaces for report rendering and access tests.
Who owns reconciliation tolerances and business acceptance.
Required evidence retention and employee consultation.
research_questions: Which failures recur often enough to justify reusable tests?
Can the existing {BI} expose filters, permissions and rendered outputs for automated checks?
Which checks require independent financial control totals?
new_work: Maintain expected results, tolerances and test data.
Investigate failed checks and distinguish defects from approved changes.
Maintain interfaces and monitor test coverage.

tasks.short: Combine financial and market trends into evidence-backed recommendations for business action.

steps.what: Retrieve current financial, customer and market datasets through the {BI} and {DATA_PLATFORM}.
Align periods and calculate financial movements and trend comparisons in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Investigate material movements and assess explanations using the {BI}.
Draft findings, options and limitations in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated trend tables, analyst driver assessment and a recommendation template.
loop.output: A recommendation draft with references, options and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Every numeric claim must match a supplied measure; unsupported explanations are flagged for analyst review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved validation failures return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and charts are deterministic; expressing varied findings and limitations requires contextual prose.

steps.what: Check evidence, uncertainty and proposed actions before sharing the brief.
Discuss trade-offs and decide whether to endorse proposed actions.
Circulate the reviewed brief and decision record through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Scheduled extracts and deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed certified measures and trend views in the {BI}. The analyst assesses drivers, and a bounded drafting loop produces a brief in the {DOCS} with traceable figures. Analyst review gates sharing; the finance manager decides on action, and the {WORKFLOW} distributes the recorded outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data preparation and repeated report writing consumed time, while inconsistent definitions made automatic summaries unreliable. Recommendations also depended on context outside the datasets.
tasks.enabler_now: Prepared semantic models, reusable calculations and source-linked drafting support the preparation work. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of stitching these components together.
tasks.still_hard: Causal explanations, changing market conditions and political or operational constraints remain difficult. Faster analysis cannot resolve missing evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Separate a measured movement from its possible causes and choose recommendations that fit business constraints.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more of the week investigating drivers and discussing options. Within an agreed remit, the analyst can prioritise investigations; spending and operational action still require the relevant manager.

reach.task: Translate working-capital movements into near-term cash scenarios.
reach.learn: Cash timing, liquidity buffers and forecast uncertainty.

reach.task: Assess which forecast assumptions should change after a material trend shift.
reach.learn: Forecast drivers, sensitivity analysis and planning governance.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 10-30 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI supports questions and report creation over semantic models, with preparation and capacity requirements.
AI/BI Genie uses trusted assets and example SQL to support governed data questions.
Uber reported faster query writing with QueryGPT and also described invented-table failures.
These examples support preparation assistance; task-level effort and build ranges remain estimates.

assumptions: The initial scope is management intelligence, with approved financial and customer measures.
The analyst supplies interpretations; the drafting loop does not independently determine causes.
Scheduled refresh is already supported and can be configured.
GDPR applies where customer or employee records enter analysis; aggregated outputs are preferred.
EU AI Act obligations depend on the eventual use; creditworthiness or employee decisions require separate assessment.
Employee consultation depends on the design and national rules.
unknowns: Quality and ownership of existing semantic models.
Source refresh schedules, licences and query access.
Approved materiality thresholds and reconciliation controls.
Whether recommendations affect regulated individual decisions.
The analyst's authority to prioritise investigations.
Approved model hosting and data processing arrangements.
research_questions: Which recurring comparisons can use certified measures without generated queries?
Can every brief figure be traced to a versioned dataset and calculation?
Which driver explanations require evidence from operational teams?
new_work: Review narrative claims, limitations and recommendations.
Investigate data-quality exceptions and unexplained movements.
Maintain certified measures, templates and validation rules.
Monitor drafting failures and source freshness.

tasks.short: Compare competitor activity, product performance and market trends to assess strategic implications.

steps.what: Retrieve licensed market datasets from a market-data service in {OTHER}.
Read competitor publications in the {DOCS} and record relevant claims.

loop.input: A fixed batch of approved competitor publications and a structured evidence schema.
loop.output: Dated product, pricing and strategy claims with source passages and uncertainty labels.
loop.check: Verify source passages and numeric tokens; the analyst approves material claims and disputed interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting evidence returns to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Publications express relevant facts in varied prose; fixed fields and keyword rules miss context and qualifications.

steps.what: Align product categories, currencies and market definitions in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate product trends and market-share movements in the {BI}.
Assess competing explanations and strategic implications in the {DOCS}.
Discuss commercial implications and endorse findings for planning.

tasks.design: Licensed feeds from {OTHER} enter the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic mappings and calculations feed market trends in the {BI}. A bounded extraction loop builds a source-linked competitor evidence register in the {DOCS}; the analyst reviews material claims and unresolved category mappings. Strategic interpretation stays with the analyst, and the finance manager endorses findings used in planning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Market sources used inconsistent categories and mixed tables with narrative publications. Maintaining comparable datasets and traceable evidence required repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable feed interfaces and reusable category mappings automate numerical preparation. Bounded extraction handles varied publications, while AI-assisted coding reduces integration cost.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor disclosures are selective, market denominators may be incomplete and apparent share movements can reflect coverage changes. Intent and strategic significance remain uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: Judge source credibility, recognise weak comparisons and distinguish competitor claims from demonstrated behaviour.

ambition.what: Choose monthly competitor-driven forecast sensitivities to investigate.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time collecting publications and rebuilding comparisons and more time testing market explanations. The analyst can prioritise research within the agreed scope; pricing and investment authority do not change.

reach.task: Assess how competitor disclosures affect commercial scenario assumptions.
reach.learn: Disclosure limitations, unit economics and scenario valuation.

reach.task: Test whether competitor price changes are plausible under current cost structures.
reach.learn: Cost drivers, product comparability and margin sensitivity.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-12; 10-30 if employee consultation is required under national rules

evidence.claim: Licensed feeds, approved category mappings and market calculations can use deterministic pipelines.
Source-linked extraction can reduce publication reading effort while leaving credibility and strategy judgments human.
The digest provides no directly matched documented case for this competitor-analysis workflow; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The company uses a limited set of licensed market sources and approved competitor publications.
Market-share calculations run only where comparable numerator and denominator data exist.
Existing {BI} measures can support the initial trend views.
Source licences permit the planned storage and processing.
GDPR applies if customer-level data enters comparisons; aggregate data is preferred.
EU AI Act obligations depend on downstream use, and employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Market source coverage, licence restrictions and feed availability.
Completeness of market denominators and historical category mappings.
Who can approve new product matches and market definitions.
Approved model processing arrangements for licensed publications.
Whether identifiable customer or employee data is involved.
Authority to prioritise competitor research and forecast sensitivities.
research_questions: Which market movements reflect changing source coverage rather than business performance?
Can approved source mappings cover most product comparisons?
Which publication claims have independent corroboration?
new_work: Review extracted claims and source references.
Resolve product mappings and changing market definitions.
Monitor feed freshness, licences and denominator coverage.
Maintain extraction schemas and validation rules.

role.altitude: The analyst's week shifts toward defining measures, investigating unexplained movements and advising finance stakeholders. Financial action and report acceptance retain their existing approval paths; broader investigation authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Budget analysis: connect market evidence to forecast assumptions.
Treasury: translate financial movements into cash scenarios.
Accounting and audit: strengthen reconciliations and report acceptance evidence.
skills_to_grow: Semantic modelling and financial measure design.
Deterministic data pipelines and regression testing.
Bounded model evaluation and evidence-linked drafting.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring financial intelligence service combining tested measures, source-linked market evidence and explicit decision options, with managers retaining authority over business action.
